section: General Knowledge & CA · Ch1 — Indian History — Deep Practice 2
subject: General Knowledge & Current Affairs
stem: Mahatma Gandhi attended only one of the three Round Table Conferences (1930-32) held in London to discuss constitutional reforms. Which one did he attend?
explanation: Gandhi attended the Second RTC (1931) as the sole Congress representative, following the Gandhi-Irwin Pact. The Congress boycotted the First and Third RTCs.

section: General Knowledge & CA · Ch1 — Indian History — Deep Practice 2
subject: General Knowledge & Current Affairs
stem: The Cripps Mission (1942), sent by the British government to secure Indian cooperation in World War II, was ultimately rejected by the Congress mainly because:

options.option_text: It did not offer immediate full self-government/independence
It offered complete immediate independence, which Congress found unacceptable
It was proposed by Gandhi himself
It abolished the British monarchy immediately

explanation: The Cripps proposals offered Dominion Status only after the war, with a right for provinces to opt out — seen as inadequate and vague, leading Gandhi to famously call it 'a post-dated cheque on a crashing bank'.

subject: General Knowledge & Current Affairs
stem: The famous 'Red Fort Trials' after independence-era events involved the trial of INA officers on charges including:
explanation: The 1945-46 Red Fort Trials charged INA officers (including Shah Nawaz Khan, Gurbaksh Singh Dhillon, Prem Sahgal) with treason/waging war against the King — the trials sparked massive public sympathy and protests across India.
